```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(robotcompR)
```

A `robot_model` is a kinematic tree: links connected by joints, rooted at a
base link. Each joint carries a fixed `origin` pose (from the parent link
frame to the joint frame), a motion along or about its `axis`, and optional
limits. Serial chains, branched trees and models read from URDF all share
the same representation, so every algorithm in the package works on all of
them.

## Building a model by hand

The child link frame of a joint is

$$
T_{\text{parent},\text{child}}(q) = T_{\text{origin}} \; M(q + q_0) \; T_{\text{post}},
$$

where $M$ is a rotation about the axis (revolute and continuous joints) or a
translation along it (prismatic joints), $q_0$ is an optional offset and
$T_{\text{post}}$ an optional fixed transform after the motion (used by the
DH builder).

```{r}
links <- list(
  robot_link("base"),
  robot_link("upper", mass = 2, com = c(0.25, 0, 0),
             inertia = inertia_rod(2, 0.5, axis = "x")),
  robot_link("lower", mass = 1, com = c(0.2, 0, 0),
             inertia = inertia_rod(1, 0.4, axis = "x"))
)
joints <- list(
  robot_joint("shoulder", "revolute", "base", "upper",
              limits = c(-pi, pi), velocity = 2, effort = 40),
  robot_joint("elbow", "revolute", "upper", "lower",
              origin = transl(0.5, 0, 0), limits = c(-2.5, 2.5))
)
arm <- robot_model(links, joints, name = "hand_built")
arm <- robot_add_frame(arm, "tool", "lower", origin = transl(0.4, 0, 0))
arm
robot_links(arm)
robot_limits(arm)
```

Queries report the structure. `robot_dof()` counts movable joints,
`robot_joint_names()` gives their order (the order of every configuration
vector), and `robot_frames()` lists every frame, including fixed ones such
as the tool:

```{r}
robot_dof(arm)
robot_joint_names(arm)
robot_frames(arm)
robot_home(arm)
robot_random_configuration(arm, n = 3, seed = 1)
```

`robot_home()` is the zero configuration projected onto the limits, and
`robot_random_configuration()` samples uniformly within them (without
touching the caller's random state when `seed` is given).

## Joint order and names

Unnamed joint vectors are positional, in `robot_joint_names()` order.
A vector or matrix whose names are exactly the joint names, each once, is
matched by name in every function, whatever its order. Partial, duplicated
or unknown names are an error instead of being used by position:

```{r}
q <- c(0.3, -0.8)
qn <- c(elbow = -0.8, shoulder = 0.3)
all.equal(robot_fk(arm, q), robot_fk(arm, qn))
Q <- rbind(c(elbow = -0.8, shoulder = 0.3), c(elbow = 0, shoulder = 1))
robot_fk_positions(arm, Q)
try(robot_fk(arm, c(shoulder = 0.3, wrist = 1)))
```

The same rule covers velocities, accelerations, efforts, torque callbacks,
path matrices, planner endpoints and trajectory columns.

Inertia helpers return tensors about the center of mass:

```{r}
inertia_box(1, c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3))
inertia_cylinder(2, radius = 0.05, length = 0.4)
inertia_sphere(1, 0.1)
```

`robot_link()` rejects inertia tensors that are not symmetric positive
semidefinite or violate the triangle inequality on the principal moments.
A violation within a relative tolerance of $10^{-9}$ is treated as roundoff
and projected onto the physical set before it is stored, so the stored
tensor never yields negative kinetic energy:

```{r}
robot_link("tip", 1, inertia = diag(c(-5e-10, 1, 1)))$inertia
try(robot_link("tip", 1, inertia = diag(c(-1e-3, 1, 1))))
```

## Denavit-Hartenberg parameters

`robot_dh()` builds a chain from standard (distal) or modified (proximal,
Craig) DH parameters. With the standard convention, each link transform is

$$
T_i = R_z(\theta_i) \, T_z(d_i) \, T_x(a_i) \, R_x(\alpha_i).
$$

With the modified convention it is
$T_i = R_x(\alpha_{i-1}) \, T_x(a_{i-1}) \, R_z(\theta_i) \, T_z(d_i)$.

```{r}
scara <- robot_dh(a = c(0.4, 0.3, 0), alpha = c(0, pi, 0), d = c(0.2, 0, 0),
                  theta = c(0, 0, 0),
                  joint_type = c("revolute", "revolute", "prismatic"),
                  limits = rbind(c(-2.5, 2.5), c(-2, 2), c(0, 0.15)),
                  name = "scara")
scara
pose_translation(robot_fk(scara, c(0, 0, 0.1)))
dh_transform(0.4, 0, 0.2, 0)
```

The PUMA 560 example uses the standard DH table of Corke (1996), in meters:

```{r}
puma <- robot_example("puma560")
puma$dh
pose_translation(robot_fk(puma, rep(0, 6)))
```

## Branched trees

```{r}
tree <- robot_example("branched")
robot_joints(tree)[, c("name", "parent", "child")]
names(robot_fk(tree, c(0.3, -0.2, 0.4, 0.1), frame = "all"))
```

## URDF import and export

`robot_read_urdf()` accepts a file path or an XML string. It supports
revolute, continuous, prismatic and fixed joints, inertials (rotated into the
link frame), and visual and collision primitives. It refuses things it
cannot represent instead of guessing:

* `xacro` files must be expanded first.
* Floating, planar and mimic joints are errors.
* Documents with entity declarations are rejected, and network access is
  disabled while parsing.
* Mesh geometry is stored by file name and never opened.
* Joint `<dynamics>` (damping and friction) is read, stored and reported
  with a warning, because the dynamics functions do not model it.

```{r}
pt <- robot_read_urdf(system.file("extdata", "pan_tilt.urdf", package = "robotcompR"))
pt
robot_joints(pt)[, c("name", "type", "lower", "upper")]
```

Exporting writes a URDF that reproduces the same kinematics and inertia.
Joint offsets are folded into the origin, and DH post transforms become an
extra fixed joint. URDF requires effort and velocity limits on revolute and
prismatic joints, and every URDF reader treats a value of 0 literally as
"no motion". The example models leave these limits unspecified, so the
export asks for the values to write through `fill_limits`:

```{r}
xml <- robot_write_urdf(robot_example("planar3"),
                        fill_limits = c(effort = 50, velocity = 5))
cat(substr(xml, 1, 600))
back <- robot_read_urdf(xml)
q <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
max(abs(robot_fk(back, q)$matrix - robot_fk(robot_example("planar3"), q)$matrix))
```

## Modifying models

Models are immutable values; modifiers return a new model.

```{r}
pose_translation(robot_fk(robot_set_end_effector(arm, "lower"), c(0, 0)))
mounted <- robot_set_base(arm, robot_pose(rotz(pi / 2), c(0, 0, 1)))
pose_translation(robot_fk(mounted, c(0, 0)))
heavier <- robot_set_inertia(arm, "lower", mass = 3, com = c(0.2, 0, 0))
robot_links(heavier)$mass
tight <- robot_set_limits(arm, rbind(c(-1, 1), c(-1, 1)))
robot_within_limits(tight, c(0.5, 1.5))
robot_clamp(tight, c(0.5, 1.5))
```
